questions.question: You hit a parked car with no one around and cannot find the owner. What should you do?

options.text: You have done everything you need to do.
You must wait for the police to arrive.
You must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
You can leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, stop and try to find the owner. If you cannot find them, leave a written note with your name, address, and details about the accident.

questions.question: When you drive faster, what happens to your field of vision?

options.text: It gets wider.
It gets narrower.
It makes it easier to see cross traffic.
It stays the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gets narrower.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the smaller your field of vision becomes. As you go faster, you see less around you. You must pay extra attention to dangers.

questions.question: When driving somewhere unfamiliar, what should you do?

options.text: Rely on road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip before you start driving.
You only need a general idea of where you are going.
Always take the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Plan your trip in advance before driving to an unfamiliar place. Check a map before you leave. Do not start driving with only a vague idea of where you are going.

questions.question: Two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads. Who must yield?

options.text: Either one
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
Neither

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right. This rule applies whether or not there are traffic signals.

questions.question: When may you use your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn when you lose control of your vehicle. This warns other drivers that something is wrong.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that show direction and distance to destinations.

options.text: Yellow
Red
Green
White

questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background. They show direction and distance to specific places. They help you when driving in unfamiliar areas.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead curves only to the right.
The road ahead turns sharply to the right.
The road ahead curves right and then left.
The road ahead curves left and then right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right and then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to hazards ahead. This yellow and black sign warns that the road will curve to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: Besides your turn signals, how can you show other drivers you plan to turn?

options.text: By your vehicle position and eye contact.
By turning your wheels.
By slowing down at the corner.
By watching the car behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: By your vehicle position and eye contact.
questions.explanation: Use your vehicle position and eye contact to show other drivers your intention to turn. This works together with your turn signals to communicate clearly.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway?

options.text: As long as you use your emergency flashers.
If no part of your car is on the road.
If you need to check a map.
Only during an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only during an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except in an emergency.

questions.question: A traffic light turns solid yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and keep going through the intersection.
Stop right away.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
Speed up to get through before the red light appears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a solid yellow light, slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing without flashing warning signals or gates, what should you do?

options.text: Cross the tracks immediately and as fast as possible.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to yield to any train at the crossing.
Speed up to cross before any oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train at the crossing.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to any train before crossing the tracks. Wait until your entire vehicle can cross safely on the other side. Do not change gears while crossing because your vehicle could stall.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
After you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Get into the exit lane early. Do not slow down until after you have moved into the exit lane.

questions.question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left, where should you look?

options.text: Over your right shoulder.
At your side mirror.
Over your left shoulder.
At your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: The intersection is blocked by other traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through completely.
Honk your horn to make cars move up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through completely.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if traffic ahead blocks your path and you cannot get all the way through. Wait until traffic clears so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: What is the most important thing to remember about speed and curves?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle may be hard to turn in curves because of inertia. To stay in control, slow down before entering the curve.

questions.question: What best keeps you and others safe when you back up your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before putting the car in reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the radio before backing up to alert people around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because drivers cannot see well behind their vehicles. Walk to the back of the vehicle before backing up to check for children and small objects.

questions.question: What is true about a work zone?

options.text: It may be moving or stationary.
It is marked with black and white signs.
It does not require you to slow down and pay extra attention.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be fixed in one place or moving, such as vehicles striping lines, mowing, or removing snow. Work zones have orange signs with black letters or symbols. Slow down and pay extra attention when you see a work zone.

questions.question: You reach an intersection with a flashing red light. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Turn right or left since the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop. Then you can go when the way is clear.

questions.question: Traffic signals use arrows to control turns from certain lanes. What does a solid yellow arrow mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a yellow circular traffic light.
It tells drivers they can turn in the direction shown.
It tells drivers a green arrow is coming soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a yellow circular traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the same as a yellow traffic light. When you see a solid yellow arrow, slow down and be ready for a red light.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly and your vehicle does not have anti-lock brakes, what should you do?

options.text: Hold down the brake pedal.
Pump your brakes firmly and quickly.
Tap the brakes lightly.
Release the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump your brakes firmly and quickly.
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best way to stop quickly in an emergency. Your car will stop fast and you can still steer.

questions.question: Your vehicle's accelerator sticks open while you are driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Blow your horn.
Slam on your brakes.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn off your ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, the engine will keep running even if you lift your foot off the gas. Turn off the ignition by moving the switch just enough to stop the engine—do not turn it so far that the steering wheel locks. Then apply your brakes and move to a safe area off the road.

questions.question: A school bus on the highway has stopped with its red lights flashing. What must you do?

options.text: Stop before reaching the bus and wait until it starts moving again.
Stop before reaching the bus and wait until the red lights stop flashing.
Stop before reaching the bus and proceed when all children have finished loading or unloading.
Stop and wait until the bus completely leaves the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before reaching the bus and wait until the red lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When you meet a stopped school bus with flashing red lights, you must stop at least 30 feet away. Do not move until the red lights stop flashing.

questions.question: How can you check your blind spots before changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Use both the inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always turn your head to check your blind spots before you change lanes.

questions.question: Highway signs that require drivers to follow an instruction are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must or must not do. If you do not follow these signs, you can be penalized.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road.
No parking.
Right lane closed.
Multiple turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that the road ahead has many curves. Slow down and be ready to turn.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and use your turn signal. Then look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: Your vehicle is in an accident and is blocking traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
Do not move your vehicle under any circumstances.
Wait for police to arrive before moving your vehicle.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the traveled part of the road if you can. Always stay at the scene and identify yourself. Offer help if needed.

questions.question: When visibility is reduced, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Turn on your windshield wipers.
Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: The first thing you should do when visibility becomes poor is to slow down. This helps you avoid accidents in bad conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must come to a complete stop and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down, be prepared to stop, and give the right-of-way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be prepared to stop, and give the right-of-way if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means yield. When you see it, slow down and be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians pass safely before you go.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
Keep your front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels sharply away from the curb. This stops your vehicle from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail. If there is no curb, turn your wheels sharply toward the edge of the road instead.
